citation: Wesolowski M, Domnicz A, Augustynowicz J, et al. VCF2CAPS - A high-throughput CAPS marker design from VCF files and its test-use on a genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) dataset
what_it_anchors: CAPS wet-lab verification: 10 markers x 30 plants each, results in prose (Results: 'Experimental verification of the identified CAPS markers', Table 1, Fig 8)
claim: Ten single-cut CAPS markers were tested on 30 plants each (10/10/10 by design); the prose reports each marker's outcome including exact matches and the markers whose predicted classes were reclassified
claim_kind: CORRECTION: the backlog previously said 'reports no wet-lab outcomes' -- that is false; it does report them, in prose. NOT tabulated: no per-marker x/30, no concordance, no error rate (Fig 8 is a gel image; the XML has no supplementary-material)

citation: Anonymised for proposal: High-efficiency 14-plex cSNP SNaPshot assay for forensic peripheral blood identification
what_it_anchors: SNaPshot detection outcome as a function of template input, and body-fluid specificity of a 14-plex cSNP panel
claim: Table S4: 14 cSNP loci, 5 RNA inputs (10/5/1/0.5/0.1 ng), 3 replicates each, allele RFU per cell; under the paper's own 100-RFU rule all 14 are detected at 10 ng and every locus fails at 0.1 ng. Table S8: 500 samples (100 each PB/MB/SE/SA/VA), 14 cSNPs detected in 100/100 PB samples, <50% in every non-blood fluid
claim_kind: quantitative outcome dataset (human forensic; not plant). 7 of the paper's 26 prose failure percentages at 0.5/0.1 ng do not reproduce from Table S4 and are recorded as a comparison

citation: Anonymised for proposal: Development of a multiplex SNaPshot assay for simultaneous detection of multiple insecticide-resistance mutations in Anopheles sinensis
what_it_anchors: SNaPshot vs PCR-Sanger genotype concordance on a non-human organism
claim: Of 272 field-collected mosquitoes, SNaPshot called 5 samples differently at vgsc (3 HN-PY + 2 AH-SC, L/F -> F/F) and 8 at Ace-1 (5 + 3, A/S -> S/S); RDL was consistent at all three sites
claim_kind: quantitative discordance counts (animal, not plant). The per-sample table the paper cites as 'Supplementary Table S5 of Additional file 3' is NOT in that file: the supplement's Table S5 is the RDL phenotype association

citation: Anonymised for proposal: Flanking Variation Influences Rates of Stutter in Simple Repeats
what_it_anchors: Stutter rate as a function of repeat length, modelled per locus
claim: Robust linear models of the -1 stutter ratio on the parental allele length (PAL) and on the longest uninterrupted stretch (LUS) at 10 simple-repeat loci; D5S818 is the only locus needing different slopes across flanking haplotypes (0.007 / 0.009)
claim_kind: CORRECTION: this file was cached as 10.1016/j.fsigen.2018.04.003 (Vilsen 2018), which is a different, closed paper (PMID 29702330, no PMCID). FORENSIC HUMAN STR: validates stutter shape only, never plant SSR behaviour
